question.text: A Fund of Funds (FoF) structure investing in other hedge funds:

answer.text: Has lower total fees than a single-strategy hedge fund
Has substantially higher fees due to double-layered management fees

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook states that FoF fees are substantially higher than those of a single-strategy hedge fund because the underlying hedge funds charge management fees and the FoF manager then charges an additional layer of management fees on top. The investor therefore bears two layers of management fees through one FoF allocation. The Trap: Total fees are not lower for an FoF — the layered structure is the whole point. FoFs are not prohibited in India, and a performance/incentive fee can still apply at either or both layers depending on the structure. Note: The fee-layering characterisation for FoF investing in other hedge funds is from the AIF (Category III) Distributors workbook (Series XIX-B).
